study.title: De Qi, a Threshold of the Stimulus Intensity, Elicits the Specific Response of Acupoints and Intrinsic Change of Human Brain to Acupuncture
study.study_design: Within-subject experimental study in healthy adult volunteers investigating intrinsic changes in the human body after acupuncture with de qi
study.population: 30 right-handed, 20–47 years old (29.0 ± 7.8), acupuncture naive healthy adult volunteers, 12 male and 18 female
study.inclusion_criteria: right-handed, 20–47 years old, acupuncture naive healthy adult volunteers
study.exclusion_criteria: major medical illnesses, history of head trauma, neuropsychiatric disorders, use of medications within one week, and contraindications for exposure to high magnetic fields

conditions.timepoint_exact: before de qi (needle in place, prior to eliciting de qi sensation)
conditions.scan_context: needle inserted and retained but de qi not yet achieved

conditions.timepoint_exact: during de qi (after de qi sensation was elicited by needle manipulation)
conditions.scan_context: needle manipulation producing de qi sensations (numbness, heaviness, distention, soreness)
basal measurement prior to needle insertion

conditions.timepoint_exact: after needle insertion but before de qi sensation
D1–D6 (up to 6 min after de qi sensation onset)
conditions.scan_context: skin blood flow measured at multiple timepoints after de qi
fMRI signal during de qi; signal intensity decreased or increased relative to before de qi

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Manual acupuncture at LI4 (Hegu) and ST36 (Zusanli) on the right extremity
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: ST.36 is located in the tibialis anterior muscle, 4 fingerbreadths below the kneecap and 1 fingerbreadth lateral from the anterior crest of the tibia. LI.4 is located in the dorsal surface of the web between the thumb and the index finger.
interventions.needle_type_exact: Disposable sterile stainless steel needles (KINGLI Medical Appliance Co., Ltd., Wuxi, China)
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.22 mm in diameter and 40 mm in length
interventions.manipulation_exact: rotated approximately 180° in each direction with even motion at the rate of one cycle per second; stimulation for 30 s at the rate of 60 times per minute with an amplitude of approximately 180° in each direction (S1–S5); 5 cycles of R-S acupuncture
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; sensitivity of the subject to needle manipulation was tested and adjusted to tolerance prior to procedure, aiming to elicit de qi sensation without noxious pain
interventions.needle_retention_exact: needle kept in place for 2 min prior to needle manipulation; needle withdrawn after completion of 5 cycles of R-S acupuncture (total approximately 300 s = 5 min)
interventions.session_duration_exact: Needle in for full paradigm: 0–300 s (5 min plus initial 2 min pre-manipulation retention)
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: subjects were instructed to lie still and keep their eyes closed during the procedure; questioned about sensations (aching, pressure, soreness, heaviness, fullness, warmth, cooling, numbness, tingling, and dull pain), sharp pain or any other sensations
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: These two acupoints were chosen because of their easy accessibility of de qi sensation and were most frequently used in acupuncture.

sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: de qi sensations: aching, pressure, soreness, heaviness, fullness, warmth, cooling, numbness, tingling, and dull pain
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: When the volunteers felt the sensations of numbness, heaviness, distention, and soreness, representing de qi
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: No validated quantitative instrument for de qi was used; sensations were assessed by verbal questioning

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: In the event of a sharp painful sensation, the needle position should be readjusted and the pain would disappear within a few seconds.
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Sharp pain was monitored and used to guide needle repositioning; not quantified

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: several volunteers felt the sensation of heat and perspiration during acupuncture manipulation, which indicated de qi
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Narrative description only; number of volunteers not specified

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 1.5-T Siemens Sonata MRI system equipped for echo planar imaging (EPI)
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: T2*-weighted gradient echo sequence; also 3D MPRAGE (magnetization-prepared rapid acquisition gradient echo) and T1-weighted high-resolution structural images
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: functional: in-plane resolution 3.125 × 3.125 mm, slice thickness 3.0 mm with 20% gap; MPRAGE: voxel size 1 mm³; T1 structural: in-plane resolution 1 × 1 mm, slice thickness 1.33 mm
statistical_thresholds_exact: not_reported explicitly; Z scores reported for each cluster/peak

extraction_notes.note: The fMRI subsample is stated as 9 subjects ('Mean results of functional MR images of brain activation/deactivation of nine subjects in each stimulation paradigm') while the overall study enrolled 30 subjects. It is unclear which 9 subjects underwent fMRI or whether all 30 participated in each sub-study (LDPI, EMG, EEG, fMRI). The n_analyzed for fMRI is inferred as 9 from the figure caption.
No sham acupuncture control group is present in this study. The study compares within-subject conditions (before de qi vs. during de qi) only. There is no sham arm.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events are not reported. Sharp pain during needling is mentioned as a reason to readjust needle position but no systematic adverse event data are provided.
Neuroimaging preprocessing and analysis software are not reported. Statistical thresholding method and multiple comparison correction for fMRI results are not stated.

The paper describes 'deep resistance' in the EMG section but provides values in uV, which is a unit of electrical potential/amplitude rather than resistance. It is unclear whether these values represent deep electrical resistance or myoelectricity amplitude. The paper uses both terms interchangeably in the same passage.

The fMRI was performed during acupuncture at ST.36, but the full paradigm involved both ST.36 and LI.4 in separate runs. The fMRI results appear to be only for ST.36 (Zusanli) based on table titles and text. No fMRI results for LI.4 (Hegu) are reported.

The paper does not clarify whether the 30 subjects all underwent all measurement modalities (LDPI, EMG, EEG, fMRI) or whether separate subgroups participated in different modalities. The fMRI appears to be n=9.
The paper states that participants provided 'verbal but not written informed consent.' This is a notable ethical reporting detail.

The y-coordinate for Posterior central gyrus activation row (act_15) is listed as 68 mm in the table, which is an unusual positive value for a posterior central region in Talairach space. This value is transcribed exactly as reported in Table 1 without modification.

The Gyrus frontalis medius deactivation row (deact_21) lists coordinates as -2, -24, 64 with hemisphere R and BA 6. A negative x-coordinate would typically suggest left hemisphere. This is transcribed exactly as reported in Table 2.
No quantitative de qi rating instrument (e.g., MASS, VAS for deqi) was used. De qi was assessed only by verbal questioning.
The number of sessions, treatment period, and practitioner qualifications are not reported.
Exact numeric blood perfusion (PU) values are visible in Figure 4 graphs but are not tabulated in the text. Only approximate percentage increase (~10%) is stated in the text.
